title: Connect durable Telegram webhook transport to the inquiry funnel

shared_paths_approval.reason: Accepted end-to-end Telegram transport slice joins the reviewed bot funnel to one authenticated HTTP adapter and requires durable replay evidence across the shared channel boundary.

requirements: Expose one injected POST /api/v1/integrations/telegram/webhook boundary. Require application/json, cap the raw body at 256 KiB, pass X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token to the existing TelegramUpdateAdapter, return safe no-store errors, and acknowledge well-formed unsupported updates without business mutation or outbound calls.

Add a Telegram transport application runtime that, for an accepted private update, ensures the trusted channel identity, invokes the existing orchestrator and renderer, acknowledges callback queries, and sends exactly one plain-text message with the reviewed inline keyboard to the trusted conversation_id. It must never accept chat_id, integration identity, method name or API base URL from user payload.

Implement an async Telegram Bot API client over the fixed official HTTPS API using an injected HTTP client and runtime-supplied token. Support only answerCallbackQuery and sendMessage, validate structured success/error responses and retry_after, use a 15 second timeout, and replace all network/provider failures with typed safe errors whose str/repr/chaining never expose the token, URL, response body, client text or Telegram description.

Extend the trusted channel persistence boundary with a read-only, privacy-preserving lookup for an already accepted event digest so a retried Telegram update after a committed SAVE, RESET or SUBMIT does not repeat a mutation or fail because the draft advanced/closed. Replays render the current safe screen for SAVE/RESET and the accepted-unconfirmed result for SUBMIT; they may repeat the outbound message and must be marked replay internally.

Keep business commit before external delivery. A provider failure returns a temporary transport error suitable for Telegram retry; a retry must use the durable event lookup and must not create another draft mutation, inquiry, receipt, audit event or notification job. Do not promise exactly-once delivery to a human.

Add route/unit tests with injected HTTP transport plus disposable PostgreSQL end-to-end tests covering first private user identity creation, start/service/requester/details/submit, callback acknowledgement before message send, inline keyboard JSON, ignored update, invalid secret/media/body/size, provider success/rate-limit/5xx/malformed response/token secrecy, and retry after simulated post-commit send failure for SAVE and SUBMIT with no duplicate business rows.

Do not register a real webhook, read real credentials, make live network calls, add environment values, change schema, implement VK, owner notifications, background jobs, polling, deployment or frontend work. Commit this exact task specification at tasks/specs/TG-015.json.
acceptance: A synthetic Telegram conversation can reach one CRM inquiry through the actual FastAPI route, PostgreSQL adapters and reviewed funnel while all Telegram HTTP is captured by an injected mock transport.
A retry after a committed mutation and failed send is safe and delivers a response without duplicating domain state.

Focused Telegram transport/webhook, channel regression, all Telegram, full pytest and whitespace gates pass; self-review verifies token secrecy, transaction/external-call ordering and exact allowed scope.
